comparison: Both evaluate SNr neuronal recording findings (C19-C25) as supported. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative assessment of sample sizes and statistical significance. Peer review describes the empirical data as 'thorough' and experiments as 'well-designed.' Both agree these core findings are solid, though peer review also includes additional claims (C26-C30, C58, C88-C90) in their evaluation.

Both evaluate probe trial and reversal experiments (C26-C30) as supported. OpenEval emphasizes the experimental design controlling for confounding variables. Peer review groups these with other neuronal recording findings and describes them as 'interesting and surprising' with thorough empirical data.

Both evaluate optogenetic tagging experiments identifying D1/D2-SPNs (C31-C34) as supported. OpenEval provides specific details about sample sizes and classification criteria. Peer review describes the methodology as part of 'thorough' empirical data with 'well-designed' experiments, grouping these with additional striatal recording claims (C59, C92-C94).

Perfect agreement on genetic knockout experiments (C35-C37, C95-C96). Both evaluate as supported. OpenEval notes appropriate controls and statistical significance while acknowledging mechanism not directly tested. Peer review describes experiments as 'well-designed' with no specific concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on pharmacological inactivation experiments (C38, C73-C74). Both evaluate as supported. OpenEval highlights within-subject design and statistical significance. Peer review describes the manipulation as part of thorough and well-designed experimental approach with no specific critiques.

Both evaluate cell-type-specific ablation experiments (C39-C41, C75, C97-C98) as supported. OpenEval emphasizes differential behavioral phenotypes and movement trajectory analysis. Peer review describes experiments as 'well-designed' and central to the manuscript's argument. Peer review also includes C61 and C65 in their evaluation.

Both evaluate D1-SPN optogenetic manipulation experiments (C42-C43, C60-C62, C76) as supported. OpenEval notes selective effects on 8s trials and linear relationship. Peer review explicitly states authors demonstrate 'a causal role for each in action selection in an opposing manner' with solid evidence. High overlap in claims (5 of 6 shared).

Perfect agreement on D2-SPN optogenetic manipulation experiments (C44-C45, C63-C64, C77). Both evaluate as supported. OpenEval notes apparent contradiction with ablation results. Peer review describes these as demonstrating causal role in action selection with thorough empirical data.

Both address the contradiction between D2-SPN ablation and inhibition results (C65, C100). OpenEval evaluates as supported, noting the contradiction is well-documented and motivates the Triple-control model. Peer review evaluates as uncertain, stating 'solid evidence' exists but 'direct evidence for a second indirect pathway is still lacking.' Peer review groups with broader model claims (C5-C6, C46-C47, C66-C67, C78-C79, C86).

Both evaluate the Triple-control model (C5-C6, C46-C47, C66-C67, C78-C79). OpenEval rates as supported, noting successful replication of experimental results but acknowledging lack of direct evidence for distinct D2-SPN subpopulations. Peer review rates as uncertain, stating the model is a 'valuable contribution' but 'lacks some direct evidence.' Key disagreement on confidence level.

Both evaluate linear relationship for D1-SPNs (C3, C81). OpenEval rates as supported, noting model predictions match experimental observations. Peer review also rates as supported, describing modeling work as part of solid evidence with thorough data. OpenEval includes additional claims (C4, C50-C51) about nonlinear D2-SPN control.

Both evaluate nonlinear control by indirect pathway (C4, C50-C51). OpenEval rates as supported, noting the distinction reconciles contradictory results but inverted-U not tested across continuous range. Peer review rates as supported, describing it as key finding distinguishing the Triple-control model with thorough data. Peer review also includes C84.

Perfect agreement on simultaneous optogenetic stimulation and recording experiments (C48, C80). Both evaluate as supported. OpenEval notes firing rate-dependent modulation supports model mechanism but sample details unclear. Peer review describes as part of thorough empirical data, though notes direct evidence for second indirect pathway still lacking.

Perfect agreement on dopamine modulation predictions (C52-C53, C85). Both evaluate as uncertain/supported with caveats. OpenEval notes model replicates previous results but inverted-U relationship not directly tested in current study. Peer review describes modeling work as solid evidence but notes some direct evidence for model components is lacking.

Both evaluate Parkinson's disease implications (C111-C112). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting these are reasonable predictions not tested experimentally. Peer review rates as supported, describing findings as 'of broad interest' with no specific concerns. Disagreement on confidence level for disease-related inferences. Peer review also includes C113 (schizophrenia).

Both evaluate schizophrenia implications (C113). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting connection is plausible but not demonstrated. Peer review rates as supported, describing findings as broadly interesting with no specific concerns. OpenEval includes additional schizophrenia claims (C55-C57, C114-C115) not in peer review evaluation.

Both evaluate summary of major findings (C58, C88-C90). OpenEval rates as supported, noting these are restatements of well-supported results. Peer review groups these with core neuronal recording findings and describes as thorough and well-designed. OpenEval includes many additional summary claims (C59, C86-C87, C91-C94).

Both evaluate summary claims about striatal subpopulations (C59, C92-C94). OpenEval rates as supported restatements of results. Peer review describes as part of thorough empirical data with well-designed experiments. OpenEval includes many additional summary claims not in this peer review evaluation.

OpenEval evaluates task design rationale and control analyses (C68-C72) as supported, noting sound logic and important controls showing neuronal dynamics reflect action selection rather than sensory/spatial factors. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretations from the model (C99, C101-C105) as supported, noting logical interpretations given model structure and results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic interpretation claims.

Both evaluate model mechanisms and alternatives (C108-C110). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting these are reasonable speculations not directly tested. Peer review also rates as uncertain, explicitly stating 'direct evidence for a second indirect pathway is still lacking.' Strong agreement that more direct evidence is needed. OpenEval includes additional claims (C106-C107) not in peer review.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge and context claims (C1-C2, C7-C18) as supported with appropriate citations. These are established facts about basal ganglia anatomy, function, and existing models. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for background claims.
